_readme: Every user-facing string in English. JSON rather than TS on purpose: scripts/generate-brand-assets.mjs runs in plain Node and reads this same file, so the Open Graph card and the page cannot drift apart. Keys must match ja.json — src/locales/index.ts types both as one shape. Asset paths and layout live in src/data/mocks/home.ts.
_stats_readme: hero.stats labels must stay unique: <HeroStats> keys its cards by label. The values are placeholders awaiting real figures — fill them in or drop the section rather than inventing numbers.

meta._ogImage_readme: Regenerate with `npm run brand` after changing the brand or hero copy — the card renders from this file. One card per locale; this is the `en` one.

_nav_readme: `path` is the page's own segment, with no locale in it. The URL is assembled by localeHref(locale, path) (src/locales/index.ts). Do not write hrefs here — that is how a locale prefix ends up doubled or missing.

underConstruction.heading: Under construction
underConstruction.body: This page is being built. It will be here shortly.

_contact_readme: `path` must match the `"contact"` entry in `nav` above. The header's link is built from `nav`; the page itself, the sitemap and the language switch use this `path`. If they drift, the header points at a 404. `heading` matches the nav label on purpose — tap "Contact", land on a page headed "Contact", the same reason the placeholder pages take their titles from the nav. `errors.*` duplicate the backend's validation, which is not redundancy: anything answerable without a round trip is answered in the browser (keep the limits in step with gc_run_functions/contact_form/main.py).

contact.heading: Contact
contact.lead: Enquiries, estimates, or a technical question
contact.body: We read everything that arrives and reply ourselves. If it is time-sensitive, say so and we will treat it that way.
contact._fields_readme: Only `message` has a placeholder. The test is whether it says something the label cannot: a sample company name is an example, not a format, and it silently picks a side on where 株式会社 goes in Japanese (this company puts it last). Name and email are fully described by their labels. A placeholder also disappears the moment someone starts typing, and whether it is announced varies by screen reader — it is not the place for a restatement of the label. `message` keeps one because "what should I write here" does not fit in a label.

message.label: Message
message.placeholder: Tell us the background, and what you are trying to make possible.

success.heading: Sent
success.body: Thank you. We will read it and reply.

errors.email: That does not look like an email address.
errors.turnstile: The check has not finished yet. Give it a moment.
errors.failed: It could not be sent. Please try again in a little while.
